title: Podium: Dedicated Provisioning & Runway Playbook for POC
summary: Workshop notes and prescriptive playbook for sizing a short-term dedicated GPU runway for customer POCs that experience highly spiky traffic. Focus on minimum viable commit, warm-pool strategies, autoscale rules, and clear cost tradeoffs across H100/A100 instance profiles.
body:
Context and goals:
- Customer: fintech startup (sandbox POC) with bursty inference from scheduled end-of-day jobs + user-triggered workflows.
- Objective: recommend a Dedicated GPU runway for an 8-week proof-of-concept that keeps 99th-pct latency below 750ms for text-generation endpoints, supports baseline traffic of ~40 rps and peak bursts to 1,200 rps for short windows, and delivers predictable monthly billing bounds for procurement.

Workshop observations (raw notes):
- Traffic pattern: steady 35-45 rps, two predictable 10–15 minute bursts per day to 600–1200 rps (batchable). Unexpected product test drove a 90-minute blast to 3k rps in staging — memory pressure was the main failure mode.
- Model target: open Llama-2-70B-int8 variant (approx perf similar to 70B quantized), KV-cache friendly. Avg response length 120 tokens, prompt prefix reuse high for feed pipelines.
- Latency SLO: 99th <= 750ms; p50 ~120ms.
- Ops constraints: customer requires VPC + private control plane trial. SLA not required, but resilient fallbacks are important.

Sizing approach (narrative):
1) Convert traffic to GPU throughput demand: estimate tokens/sec and tokens per GPU/sec. Use empirical model bench profiles from runtime team.
2) Add safety headroom: warm-pool reserve, prewarm windows, and scale-up latency budget.
3) Generate 3 commit options: minimal (trial credit-friendly), balanced (recommended), and gold (robust).
4) Define autoscale and fallback policies to avoid cold-start failures during rare extreme blasts.

Key assumptions and performance inputs (from bench data):
- Llama-2-70B-int8 on H100-80GB: ~1,100 tokens/sec per GPU at 128-context, steady-state generation workload (contiguous tokens).
- Same model on A100-80GB: ~650 tokens/sec per GPU.
- Average tokens generated per request: 120 tokens (incl prompt + completion).
- Average tokens consumed for prefix reuse caching: 25% saved on repeat flows.
- Warmup cold-start penalty: 4–9s to populate KV cache depending on sequence length.

Traffic conversion example (baseline numbers):
- Baseline request rate: 40 rps * 120 tokens = 4,800 tokens/sec.
- Peak burst: 1,200 rps * 120 = 144,000 tokens/sec.
- Effective tokens/sec after cache reuse (10% reuse baseline, 40% reuse for chat-like flows): conservative assume 15% reuse overall.

Commit scenarios (three options):
1) Minimal trial (cost-min): A100-fallback focused, small warm-pool
   - Compute: 3 A100-80GB GPUs dedicated (reserve) + autoscale up to 8 GPUs on demand
   - Effective tokens/sec reserve: 3 * 650 = 1,950 t/s -> supports ~16 rps steady at 120 tokens (safety headroom low)
   - Expected monthly cost (est): $3,200–$5,400 (includes partial reserved discount window assumptions)
   - Risks: will need frequent autoscale for bursts; longer scale-up times, higher chance of cold-start latency violations.

2) Balanced (recommended): mixed fleet with warm-pool
   - Compute: 4 H100-80GB GPUs reserved as warm-pool + autoscale group of H100s to 12 total for burst absorption
   - Reserve tokens/sec: 4 * 1,100 = 4,400 t/s -> supports ~36 rps baseline comfortably and handles moderate bursts with autoscale buffer
   - Warm-pool policy: keep 2 GPUs fully warmed (lowest latency), 2 GPUs in medium standby (quick warm-up path)
   - Expected monthly cost (est): $22,000–$28,000 (includes reserved instance discount, buffer for partial hours)
   - Benefits: predictable latency, reduced cold penalty, simpler fallback to A100 variants if needed.

3) Gold (high-availability): high commit, comfortable headroom
   - Compute: 8 H100-80GB reserved + autoscale to 16 for headroom
   - Reserve tokens/sec: 8 * 1,100 = 8,800 t/s -> baseline and large bursts within SLO without immediate autoscale
   - Expected monthly cost (est): $42,000–$52,000
   - Use case: sustained high throughput or enterprise POC where procurement budgets allow.

Autoscaling policy recommendations (practical rules):
- Scale-up trigger: sustained queue depth increase OR tokens/sec crossing >75% of warm-pool capacity for 12s window. Use a token-based metric rather than raw rps.
- Scale-up step: add one H100 node per 6s evaluation, until max group size. Prefer small, rapid increments to avoid overshoot.
- Prewarm strategy: when scale path is initiated for a burst forecast (from product signal), pre-create containers with empty KV cache and a single synthetic prefix to cut cold-start in half.
- Scale-in cooldown: 5–10 minutes minimum after scale-down trigger to avoid flapping during noisy bursts.
- Warm-pool sizing: maintain at least 25% of baseline capacity in warmed nodes for chat-heavy workloads. For batch-heavy, smaller warm-pool is OK.

Fallback & graceful degradation patterns:
- Model-tier fallback: have an A100-quantized variant available in lower-cost lane to accept degraded throughput with higher latency but maintain availability.
- Response shedding: implement token-budget gating at request ingress to return quick partial responses when queue grows beyond threshold.
- Region fallback: route bursts to second region dedicated pool if inter-region network policy allows and latency target permits.

Cost estimation methodology (how numbers were derived):
- Start with cloud GPU list price (public market) and apply typical reserved / committed discount ranges (20–50% depending on term).
- Add networking, storage, and control-plane overhead (approx 8–12% of GPU cost).
- Multiply by operational buffer for autoscale churn (5–12% depending on burstiness).
- Round to ranges to reflect uncertainty and negotiation levers.

Runway and contract guidance for POC (procurement-friendly):
- Recommend 3-month minimum for balanced option to ensure enough telemetry for final sizing decisions.
- Offer month-to-month for minimal trial but with soft limits for concurrency to avoid cost explosion.
- If customer wants buy-in: propose 6–12 month commitment with step-down clauses tied to usage metrics.

Operational playbook (actions during POC):
- Week 0: provision reserved warm-pool according to chosen scenario; deploy runtime with tracing and token-level billing hooks.
- Week 1: Synthetic stress tests to validate autoscale triggers; iterate thresholds.
- Week 2–4: Onboard customer traffic; enable gradual canary for production endpoints.
- Week 5: Mid-POC workshop to review telemetry and propose scale adjustments or commit changes.
- Week 7: Draft final sizing recommendation and procurement worksheet.

Quick runbook for burst day (example):
- T-30m: if product flag shows scheduled job, ensure warm-pool at 100% and prewarm span for 10m.
- T-5m: lock-in autoscale upper bound and enable dedicated tracing.
- T+0: monitor token/sec; if observed >85% of reserve, let autoscale run with max 2 node adds per minute.
- Post-burst: hold scaled capacity for 10 min then begin scale-in cooldown.

Open questions & risks (needs engineering follow-up):
- Verify H100 tokens/sec estimates for our exact container image and optimizer flags; current numbers are bench approximations.
- Need a prewarming library integration that reduces cold-start KV fill time further; ticket created in JIRA-SE-7812.
- Validate inter-region data ingress costs if we recommend region fallback for availability.
- Confirm security and KMS path for private VC deployment in POC timeline.

Action items (owners):
- Elena: finalize cost worksheet and send to sales (by 2025-03-07).
- Miguel: spin up balanced-profile cluster in staging and run 3 canonical stress tests (by 2025-03-05).
- Priya: draft customer-facing one-pager with commit scenarios and procurement language (by 2025-03-06).

Appendix (short tables and quick reference):
GPU profile quick reference:
- H100-80GB: ~1,100 t/s (70B-int8), high perf, higher $/hr.
- A100-80GB: ~650 t/s (70B-int8), lower perf, cheaper $/hr.

Sample quick-calculation cheat-sheet (copyable):
1) tokens_per_sec_needed = rps * avg_tokens_per_request
2) gpus_needed_raw = tokens_per_sec_needed / tokens_per_gpu_sec
3) gpus_reserved = ceil(gpus_needed_raw * 1.25) // 25% headroom

Notes-to-self style fragments (raw):
- Customer asked about spot capacity: ok for non-prod but not for warm-pool.
- Consider multi-model routing: short responses -> smaller LLMs to save tokens.
- Document should be lightweight version for AE to present in kickoff call.

End of document.
estimates_table:
Scenario | Reserved GPUs | Autoscale cap | Est monthly cost (range)
Minimal | 3 A100 | 8 | $3.2k - $5.4k
Balanced | 4 H100 reserved (2 warmed) | 12 | $22k - $28k
Gold | 8 H100 | 16 | $42k - $52k

(Assumptions: token/sec profiles from runtime bench, storage+network overhead 10%)
